v1.feedback: tracePaths() only traces individual quarter-circle arcs per tile — particles loop on tiny isolated arcs instead of flowing through connected labyrinthine routes across tile boundaries. Fix by following arc endpoints into neighboring tiles to build long continuous strands; this is what would make the piece read as 'routing' rather than a static texture. The palette (sienna/parchment/ash/charcoal) is well-chosen, but the form is entirely flat with negligible Y variation — consider extruding path density into subtle topography or layering strands at different heights so the labyrinth reads with more depth from the angled camera. The chain lineage from mvh (disrupt_the_grid) is invisible; there should be residual evidence of grid disruption — e.g. tiles that fracture or warp away from the regular tiling — to show the parent form after the word passed through it.
